title: Dummy dehydration order-flow teaching case
opening: A synthetic 30-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after two days of vomiting, dizziness, and reduced oral intake.
appearance: The patient is awake, tired, and mildly dehydrated.

history.History of Present Illness: The patient has vomited six times and has been unable to keep fluids down for two days.
history.Review of Systems: No chest pain, bleeding, focal weakness, or fever.

exam.Skin: Dry mucous membranes and reduced skin turgor.
exam.Neuro/Psych: Alert and oriented without focal deficits.

clinicalStates.appearance: The patient remains tired and mildly dehydrated.
The patient is comfortable, alert, and no longer dizzy.
clinicalStates.progressNote: Dizziness and tachycardia resolve after intravenous fluid replacement.

clinicalStates.appearance: The patient is weak, confused, and hypotensive.
clinicalStates.progressNote: Volume depletion has worsened with hypotension and confusion.

orders.name: Counseling, oral hydration and return precautions

orderBehaviors.notification: The patient's dizziness resolves and vital signs improve after the saline bolus.

orderBehaviors.progressNote: The patient remains nauseated and cannot tolerate enough oral fluid for rapid replacement.

orderBehaviors.notification: The patient becomes hypotensive and confused after additional fluid loss.

results.value: Sodium 148 mEq/L; potassium 3.4 mEq/L; bicarbonate 20 mEq/L; BUN 30 mg/dL; creatinine 1.2 mg/dL.

transitionRules.notification: Without effective fluid replacement, the patient becomes hypotensive and confused.

transitionRules.progressNote: Peripheral IV access is established and a normal saline bolus is administered.
The improved patient is discharged with hydration instructions and return precautions.

scoreRules.label: Perform focused cardiovascular examination
scoreRules.rationale: The examination helps identify tachycardia and poor volume status.

scoreRules.label: Evaluate electrolytes and renal function
scoreRules.rationale: Vomiting and dehydration can cause electrolyte abnormalities and prerenal kidney injury.

scoreRules.label: Establish IV access
scoreRules.rationale: IV access enables rapid fluid replacement.

scoreRules.label: Administer isotonic intravenous fluid
scoreRules.rationale: Isotonic fluid treats symptomatic volume depletion.

scoreRules.label: Monitor the tachycardic patient
scoreRules.rationale: Monitoring supports reassessment during rapid fluid replacement.

scoreRules.label: Provide hydration instructions and return precautions
scoreRules.rationale: Discharge education supports continued recovery and recognition of deterioration.

scoreRules.label: Choose home disposition after improvement
scoreRules.rationale: A stable patient who has improved may complete recovery at home with precautions.

scoreRules.label: Avoid unnecessary abdominal CT
scoreRules.rationale: There are no focal findings requiring abdominal CT in this synthetic case.

scoreRules.label: Avoid diuretic administration during dehydration
scoreRules.rationale: A diuretic worsens this patient's volume depletion.

feedback: This synthetic teaching case demonstrates how global orders, case-specific results, patient-state changes, simulated time, harmful actions, and score rules work together. It is software-validation content and not clinical guidance.
